redFlags.text: Sudden severe testicular pain or swelling
redFlags.why: Possible testicular torsion — testis can be lost within ~6 hours.

redFlags.text: New lump or hardness in a testis
redFlags.why: Must exclude testicular cancer (most common cancer in men 15–40).

redFlags.text: Blood in semen that persists, or any blood in semen over age 40
redFlags.why: Needs exclusion of prostate / urinary tract pathology.

redFlags.text: Painful, swollen scrotum with fever or discharge
redFlags.why: Possible epididymo-orchitis / infection — early antibiotics prevent obstruction.

redFlags.text: New breast enlargement with low libido / small testes
redFlags.why: Possible hormonal disorder (e.g., Klinefelter, prolactinoma, steroid use).

redFlags.text: Stopped steroids/testosterone and symptoms of crash (fatigue, low mood, no libido)

redFlags.why: Infertility distress is real; immediate human support.
